From 82d1f01292d3f09bf063f829f8ab8de12b4280a1 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Marco Elver <elver@google.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 13:47:26 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] vmalloc: fix buffer overflow in vrealloc_node_align()

Commit 4c5d3365882d ("mm/vmalloc: allow to set node and align in
vrealloc") added the ability to force a new allocation if the current
pointer is on the wrong NUMA node, or if an alignment constraint is not
met, even if the user is shrinking the allocation.

On this path (need_realloc), the code allocates a new object of 'size'
bytes and then memcpy()s 'old_size' bytes into it.  If the request is to
shrink the object (size < old_size), this results in an out-of-bounds
write on the new buffer.

Fix this by bounding the copy length by the new allocation size.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/20260420114805.3572606-2-elver@google.com
Fixes: 4c5d3365882d ("mm/vmalloc: allow to set node and align in vrealloc")
Signed-off-by: Marco Elver <elver@google.com>
Reported-by: Harry Yoo (Oracle) <harry@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Uladzislau Rezki (Sony) <urezki@gmail.com>
Acked-by: Vlastimil Babka (SUSE) <vbabka@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Harry Yoo (Oracle) <harry@kernel.org>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>

diff --git a/mm/vmalloc.c b/mm/vmalloc.c
index aa08651ec0df..c31a8615a832 100644
--- a/mm/vmalloc.c
+++ b/mm/vmalloc.c
@@ -4361,7 +4361,7 @@ void *vrealloc_node_align_noprof(const void *p, size_t size, unsigned long align
 		return NULL;
 
 	if (p) {
-		memcpy(n, p, old_size);
+		memcpy(n, p, min(size, old_size));
 		vfree(p);
 	}
 
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies a single file, `mm/vmalloc.c`, to fix a buffer overflow bug in the `vrealloc_node_align_noprof` function.

### Modifications in `mm/vmalloc.c`
- **Line 4364**: Changed the `memcpy` call from `memcpy(n, p, old_size);` to `memcpy(n, p, min(size, old_size));`. This ensures that the bytes copied into the newly allocated buffer are bounded by the new allocation size (`size`) when shrinking the object, preventing an out-of-bounds write.

### Relationships
The bug occurs when the function decides to allocate a new buffer (due to NUMA node or alignment mismatch) and the request is to shrink the object (`size < old_size`). Previously, the copy length (`old_size`) could exceed the new buffer's capacity, causing a buffer overflow. The fix aligns the copy length with the smaller of the two sizes, ensuring only valid memory is copied and eliminating the overflow.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
- `memcpy(n, p, old_size);`
Reason:
When the function executes the `need_realloc` path (due to NUMA node or alignment mismatch) while the user is shrinking the allocation (`size < old_size`), a new buffer of `size` bytes is allocated. Then `memcpy()` copies `old_size` bytes from the old buffer into the new buffer, causing an out-of-bounds write because the new buffer is only `size` bytes.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
- `memcpy(n, p, min(size, old_size));`
Reason:
By limiting the copy length to the minimum of `size` (new allocation size) and `old_size` (previous allocation size), the copy never exceeds the bounds of the new buffer. This prevents the buffer overflow when shrinking a reallocation that is forced by NUMA node or alignment constraints.
